subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted API vs current provider) - follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs (p95/p99) - recap & next steps

Thanks for the call earlier, Alex — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned on the performance qualification work.

Recap of Finlytics targets from the call:
- End-to-end p95 latency target: <= 1.2s (1200 ms)
- End-to-end p99 latency target: <= 2.2s (2200 ms)
- Typical request size: 150-350 tokens in, expected response 50-300 tokens
- Concurrency target for steady-state: ~300 concurrent open sessions; burst to 800 for short windows
- Throughput: target ~600-1,200 RPS during business hours (avg 800 RPS)
- Streaming requirement: partial token streaming for UI update, client expects first-byte partial tokens within 200-300 ms for short responses

As discussed, what we specifically need from you to qualify performance end-to-end (hosted API vs your current provider):
1) Current provider (ProviderX) measured end-to-end p95/p99 numbers (include any details on how you measure — client-side or from their edge).
2) Typical payload sizes and a few representative prompts (so we can reproduce).
3) Peak concurrency windows and a recent spike example (timestamp + approximate RPS).
4) Whether p95/p99 targets must include your client-side network (our baseline tests exclude customer WAN latency unless you ask otherwise).

Next steps I propose:
- You send the ProviderX numbers and sample prompts (item 1 & 2) — ideally by EOD tomorrow.
- Redwood will run a 48-hour benchmark (hosted API) using mirror traffic and your prompts; we’ll produce p95/p99, throughput, and concurrency sensitivity matrix.
- If numbers look good, small pilot (2 weeks) with real traffic and a mutual action plan + SLAs.

I attached the call recording and a short analysis sheet with baseline assumptions. I’ll draft a mutual-action-plan doc and share it after we see ProviderX numbers.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs (p95/p99) - recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear summary. Below are the numbers we have from ProviderX for our typical traffic shape (these are measured from our frontend to ProviderX endpoint, so they include our WAN and browser overhead):

ProviderX (current) - observed over last 30 days (avg daytime traffic):
- End-to-end p95: ~950 ms
- End-to-end p99: ~1,850 ms
- Typical concurrency during peak window: ~500 concurrent open sessions (we measure sessions differently but this maps to ~650 RPS average during the 30-minute peak)
- Burst observed: up to ~1,200 RPS for ~3-5 minutes (we see a spike like this ~1-2x/week)
- Streaming: ProviderX supports streaming but in our implementation we see chunking delays; first-token tends to arrive at ~400-600 ms for 50–100 token replies (we suspect their internal batching contributes).

We’ll attach a short CSV export of recorded latencies and a couple of sample prompts you can use to reproduce. For the prompts, the expected output lengths are included in the CSV.

We do want the p95/p99 numbers to reflect end-to-end user experience (i.e., include client-side network). If you run tests without the client network, please provide an adjustment or add a note so we can map numbers.

We’re happy to share a time slot for the pilot next week.

—Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 13:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs (p95/p99) - hosted baseline & test plan

Perfect — thanks for the CSV and the prompts, Alex. Quick notes from our side after a first pass with mirror traffic (internal non-production baseline):

Redwood hosted baseline (internal quick run, short answers ~<150 tokens):
- Observed end-to-end p95: ~780 ms
- Observed end-to-end p99: ~1,450 ms
- These results are from our hosted API in us-west; these runs included simulated client-side latency of ~60 ms to better approximate your WAN.

Observations & clarifying questions:
- Token count sensitivity: latency grows ~+120–200 ms when response size crosses ~250 tokens due to decoder loop and network streaming; do you expect many responses >250 tokens?
- Streaming expectations: you asked for first-byte partial tokens within 200–300 ms. In our hosted baseline we can hit ~200–250 ms for short responses under steady load, but bursts and long outputs increase first-byte time. We recommend enabling continuous streaming flag and a small max-response-chunk size to improve first-byte times.
- Concurrency: we can sustain 800 concurrent sessions with p95 target of ~900 ms if we optimize batching/queueing. For strict p99 <= 2.2s at burst rates (1k+ RPS), we may need reserved capacity (Dedicated) or a routing policy to fallback to a smaller model for long responses.

Proposed short mutual action plan (attached as a doc):
1) Redwood runs a 48-hour hosted test using your sample prompts + mirror traffic (we’ll include client-side emulation).
2) We’ll provide detailed p50/p95/p99 breakdowns by prompt length bucket and by concurrency bucket.
3) If we hit your p95/p99 targets in hosted, we move to a 2-week pilot (production traffic) and instrument deeper traces. If we don’t, we’ll propose Dedicated config (reserved capacity + burst buffer) and tuning recommendations.

Can you confirm:
- Which prompt bucket should be prioritized (short answers vs long summaries)?
- A couple of 1–2 hour test windows next week that work for your SRE to observe?

I attached a draft mutual-action-plan doc and the quick baseline spreadsheet. If you’re good, I’ll schedule the 48-hour run for Mon-Tue next week.

Thanks —
Marissa
